question: In which year did India adopt a dual exchange rate for the interim period?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India adopted a dual exchange rate system on March 1, **1992**.
 
• The system was introduced as part of the economic reforms initiated by the government to stabilize the Indian economy.
 
• This system is also known as the Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS).
 
• Under LERMS, 40% of foreign exchange earnings were to be surrendered at the official rate, and the remaining 60% were to be converted at market-determined rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dual Exchange Rate System**

 
 
• A dual exchange rate system is where a country's currency has multiple exchange rates for different transactions. This can help stabilize the economy during transition periods.
 
• It allows the government to manage the official exchange rate while letting market forces determine the other rate, providing a balance between control and flexibility.
 
 
 
• **Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS)**
 
 
• LERMS was introduced in 1992 as part of India's economic liberalization.
 
• It aimed to gradually move towards a market-determined exchange rate system while maintaining some control over foreign exchange.
 
• This system was a transitional arrangement before fully adopting a unified exchange rate system.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms of 1991-1992**
 
 
• The Indian government initiated comprehensive economic reforms in 1991-1992 to combat a severe balance of payments crisis.
 
• These reforms included liberalization of the economy, reduction of tariffs, deregulation of markets, and opening up to foreign investment.
 
• The introduction of LERMS was a key part of these reforms, aimed at improving foreign exchange reserves and stabilizing the economy.
